headline: Closed the page-crash that a NaN could cause in every game
lede: One title's physics can emit a NaN, and a NaN handed to the Web Audio layer throws instead of going silent — a page error that can stall a frame loop. The shared audio controller now catches it at the source, for every title, with a harness that proves it can fail.

notes.text: AudioController rejects non-finite frequency/duration/volume/level args at every scheduling entry point; a malformed cue is dropped (and does not count as feedback) instead of crashing the caller. A NaN pan still falls back to mono, so valid-sounding cues never change.

New `npm run audiocheck` drives the whole public API against a Chrome-faithful fake AudioContext that rejects non-finite exactly like the browser — 14/14, self-proving: remove any guard and the matching NaN call throws red. Registered in the core CI scope.

The #601 freeze held all session (main red on the #2145 papersplay-ink family). PR #2166 is complete and its required `static` check is green — it is parked, merge held until a green nightly lifts the freeze.

look.text: Defender — the hum whose NaN this fix catches
